title: Service Strip Prescription
subject: Real Property
stem: After Stephen demanded removal of a locked equipment cage from a paved service strip, Priscilla refused. Stephen held a recorded easement to drive service vans over the strip across Priscilla's repair-shop parcel to reach a rear storage building. Eleven years earlier, Priscilla had bolted a locked roll-down gate across the strip and built a compressor enclosure on it, using the area as part of her machine shop. Stephen knew about the gate and enclosure but did not use the strip or object. The jurisdiction recognizes extinguishment of easements by prescription, and the prescriptive period is eight years.

choices.A: The easement continues because nonuse alone cannot terminate an easement, even when the servient owner has obstructed the route.
choices.B: Priscilla automatically acquires Stephen's benefited parcel because she blocked the service strip.
choices.C: The easement may be extinguished because Priscilla's open, adverse obstruction prevented use for longer than the prescriptive period.
choices.D: The easement necessarily continues because a recorded easement cannot be lost by prescription.

rightExplanation: The easement may be extinguished. Nonuse by the dominant owner, standing alone, does not ordinarily terminate an easement. But some jurisdictions recognize extinguishment by prescription when the servient owner openly and adversely prevents use of the easement for the full prescriptive period. Priscilla did more than leave the strip unused. She locked a gate across it, built an enclosure on it, and used the area as part of her shop for eleven years. Stephen knew of the obstruction and did not act. That period exceeded the eight-year prescriptive period.

wrongExplanations.A: The nonuse rule is attractive because Stephen simply failed to use the strip for years. The breaker is that Priscilla also made an open, adverse obstruction for the full prescriptive period.
wrongExplanations.B: The obstruction facts suggest a property-right shift. The breaker is that prescription here may extinguish the easement; it does not transfer Stephen's benefited parcel to Priscilla.
wrongExplanations.D: Recording makes the easement visible and enforceable against later owners. The breaker is that recording does not protect an easement from later termination by a recognized prescription doctrine.
